reference_sql:
SELECT product_id, valid_from, valid_to - valid_from + 1 AS days_applied
FROM cost_history
WHERE valid_to IS NOT NULL
alternatives: SELECT product_id, valid_from, date_diff('day', valid_from, valid_to) + 1 AS days_applied FROM cost_history WHERE valid_to IS NOT NULL
SELECT product_id, valid_from, CAST(valid_to + INTERVAL 1 DAY AS DATE) - valid_from AS days_applied FROM cost_history WHERE valid_to IS NOT NULL

other_way.sql: SELECT product_id, valid_from, date_diff('day', valid_from, valid_to) + 1 AS days_applied FROM cost_history WHERE valid_to IS NOT NULL
other_way.tradeoff: date_diff('day', valid_from, valid_to) + 1 gives the same count, and its unit argument says plainly that days are counted.
